newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds' correction seen benign.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - U.S. T-bonds' correction seen benign.

text.p: A pullback in U.S. Treasury bond futures that began earlier in the week after a 2-1/2 month rally is likely to be short-lived and relatively benign, technical analysts said.
Elliott Wave watchers said the market might already be approaching a near-term bottom, depending on where the wave-count starts.
"Short-term, I think we're bottoming today or tomorrow...somewhere between where we are now (mid-111s) and 110-23/32," said David Lockwood, senior interest rate analyst at Elliott Wave International.
September T-bond futures were drifting in the mid-111 area, off about a quarter point on the day and down from last Friday's 112-24/32 four-month high.
"I'm thinking it's a small-degree fourth wave," Lockwood said.
His short-term five-wave sequence started from the May 27 low, where the market's uptrend from early April lows inflected steeply upward.
Should the market put in a near-term bottom here, he said, it would likely make new highs above last Friday's 112-24/32 peak soon, though probably not much above it.
He expected the market to continue churning for a while and said no clear upside target was projected for now.
John Gambino of JBG Technical Analysis saw a slightly deeper correction, citing a longer-term wave-count.

"We've finished a five-wave sequence up (from April lows)," he said. "Looking at the big picture, this is only one of a series of five-wave upmoves...but now that we've finished the first one, it's entitled to a correction."
He said a pullback of 50 percent, or even 62 percent, would not be unusual and that he would look to re-establish long positions in the 109-10/32 to 108-1/2 area.
He said a bottoming in the 111 to 111-12/32 area was possible using counts from the May 27 low, but he preferred the intermediate-term count from the April lows.
Besides the Elliott Wave projections, analysts saw various factors suggesting limited losses during the current down leg.

Matthew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group, said the overbought conditions in daily oscillators, which had been putting a brake on the market's uptrend for the past week or so, were being resolved.
He said the daily stochastic had moved out of overbought levels and was refreshing itself in neutral territory.
He added that, from a fundamental point of view, the market was likely to be entrenched in a range-trade mode going into the Federal Open Market Committee meeting next Tuesday and Wednesday.

Further, recent declines in commodity prices were also supportive, he noted. The Commodity Research Bureau index .CRB fell nearly six percent from its late May peak of 254.79 to a low earlier in the week of 239.77.
"That's a very powerful fundamental positive," he said. He did not expect the current down move to go much below 111.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
